summary: CMP-1 mobile parity (mobile/app/complaints.tsx) verified end-to-end via Expo web preview as cathy@example.com. Complaints list loads (2 seed rows), 4-step wizard opens & advances, required-field gating works, elder_abuse selection shows/hides cmp1-new-elder-safeguard, POST /api/cmp1/participants/{pid}/complaints returns 200 and a new cmp1-row-* appears, ACQSC form toggles and POST /submit-to-acqsc returns 200 with an audit-trail entry rendered by cmp1-acqsc-trail-list-*, submission history 'DELIVERED to info@agedcarequality.gov.au' shows correctly. All required data-testids present. No red screen, no console errors.
action_items: OPTIONAL — investigate whether GET /api/cmp1/participants/{pid}/complaints returns evidence_bundle_id in the list payload. During this run cmp1-bundle-pdf-* count was 0 across 3 rows (2 pre-existing + 1 newly-created). The mobile screen only renders the link when c.evidence_bundle_id is truthy, so if the API omits/nulls it in list mode the PDF affordance never appears (functional but not verifiable in this env). Confirm web ComplaintsList.jsx shows the same result for the same participant — if web shows the link and mobile does not, that's a parity gap; otherwise both behave identically.
critical_code_review_comments: Minor: /app/mobile/app/complaints.tsx line 174 uses process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL directly for the bundle PDF URL. Works via Linking.openURL but bypasses the apiFetch auth header — if the /export.pdf endpoint requires bearer auth the mobile deep-open may 401. Web uses <a href> under the browser session; mobile has no session cookie in Linking. Consider using a signed short-lived URL or expo-web-browser with headers.
Info: LInput uses TextInput; keyboardType for provider_email is not set to 'email-address' (line 308) — minor UX polish for mobile.

Info: RN Web renders disabled Pressable as aria-disabled=true (not native disabled). Playwright is_disabled() returns False. Not a bug — verified visual + behavioural gating via aria-disabled attribute.
